summary: Iter-34 tests both master + granular locks and the new generic edit-request. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_iter34_master_and_granular_locks.py — 16/16 passed (POST /apps/{id}/locks/all, POST /locks/item with 400 on unknown kind, 403 for editor on lock-all + lock-item, GET /apps/{id}/locks, GET /locks/summary, GET /edit-access for owner/editor, 423 gates on CMS item PUT, workflow PUT and DELETE, owner can save while all-locked, generic POST /edit-request → approve → single-use grant consumed → re-lock, no route-shadowing between /locks/all vs /locks/item and page vs generic edit-access). Frontend Playwright: admin sees master-lock-btn in header on every tab (Overview/Site/CMS/Workflows) plus duplicate master control on Overview via overview-master-lock; Lock all flips to Unlock all with counter 28/28, badge switches to 'Fully locked', reverses instantly to 0/28 'Unlocked' with no confirm dialog. Lock state persists across full page reload (POST /locks/all responses stick and refresh via GET /locks). Granular locks render as expected: lock-block-*/lock-form-* (7 in Site Mode outline), lock-cms_collection-* (2), lock-cms_item-* (1), lock-workflow-* (3), lock-overview-default, lock-app_mode-default. Locking a single workflow flips header badge to 'Partially locked'. Dashboard shows lock-badge chips per tenant card. Editor sees no master-lock-btn (correct) and sees lock-state-badge/master-lock-badge instead.

minor.issue: Response 'locked' field is overwritten by summary's integer locked-count instead of echoing the requested boolean (harmless: frontend reads the 'locks' map). Consider spreading summary first, then echoing body fields last.

ui_bugs.issue: On the Overview tab there are TWO elements with the same data-testid=master-lock-btn (header MasterLockButton + the one nested inside overview-master-lock container). Playwright must use .first / narrow scope. Not a functional bug but a testability smell.

issues: Header renders LockStateBadge right next to MasterLockButton — both pills look visually similar ('Unlocked' badge and 'Lock all 0/28' button share pill styling), can feel redundant. Consider hiding the badge when the button already conveys the state, or restyling one.

action_items: (optional) De-duplicate data-testid=master-lock-btn on the Overview tab so Playwright can query without .first — e.g. give the Overview instance its own testid or ensure the header one is the only one on that tab.
(optional) Swap ordering in /locks/item response so body.locked (bool) is preserved and not overwritten by summary's locked-count int.
critical_code_review_comments: locks.apply_all + lock_item both spread summary AFTER the boolean 'locked' echo, so 'locked' silently changes type in the response payload. Low risk today but a landmine if the FE ever reads r.data.locked as a bool.

MasterLockButton is embedded inside OverviewPanel's overview-master-lock container, which means two DOM nodes carry data-testid=master-lock-btn on the Overview tab — violates unique-testid convention.

edit_requests.active_grant looks up by (app_id, page_id, user_id) where page_id is used as a generic item_id for CMS items/workflows too. It works because the field is just a string key, but the naming is misleading; renaming to item_id (or aliasing) would future-proof the code.
locks.assert_item_editable imports edit_requests.active_grant lazily inside every call — fine for now, but a top-level import would be cleaner and avoid repeated attribute lookups on hot paths.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all key data-testids present and interactive; two minor testability/design nits)
